covariate_support_check.evidence: real 400: Named argument holiday_region not found in signature for call to function AI.FORECAST
covariate_support_check.conclusion: AI.FORECAST owns the nightly baseline forecast only; the approve-time re-forecast and festival/promo covariates stay on ARIMA_PLUS_XREG (03_forecast_arima_xreg.sql) and the local model.

sql_bug_found_and_fixed.symptom: Required field date cannot be null (400 BadRequest)
sql_bug_found_and_fixed.cause: AI.FORECAST called over every (sku,cluster_id) pair with no minimum-history filter; a series too short to forecast returns a null forecast_timestamp, which then fails the INSERT NOT NULL constraint on taal.forecasts.date
sql_bug_found_and_fixed.fix: added a qualifying_series temp table (HAVING COUNT(*) >= 28), same threshold jobs/sense/backtest.py and the ARIMA_PLUS_XREG job use

known_leftover: One earlier duplicate full-scale test run (run_id=ai_forecast_timesfm_20260927T144308Z, 25060 rows) was left in the shared taal.forecasts table, because DELETE FROM taal.forecasts failed with a real 403 (billingNotEnabled). This is NOT transient and NOT unrelated: this project (amru-509214) has no billing account enabled, and BigQuery's free tier rejects every DML statement (DELETE confirmed directly against an unrelated table too; MERGE is also DML and almost certainly blocked the same way) while SELECT and INSERT both work. See eval/raw/bigquery_billing_dml_2026-09-27/finding.json for the full, independently-confirmed writeup -- this is a project-level billing-account gap, not an IAM role gap, and it blocks 04_rolldown.sql's DELETE and every agents/gate/bigquery_store.py write() call, not just this cleanup attempt.
